beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 1/4 - ClaudeComposerAsk. Reconstructed prompt, said aloud to be a reconstruction. Liam named in the first breath.
beats.narration_text: Sawubona - this is Liam, in for Bear. The prompt on screen is a reconstruction, written to be illustrative. It is not a transcript. The game under it is real: a dungeon slice in Godot four. What we are taking apart today is not the game logic. It is three hand-written shaders, and one stubborn question - what does a hint actually do to a number.

props.topic: WALKER - GODOT SHADERS AND MATERIALS TEARDOWN
props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about The Lost - a side-view dungeon crawler where every hazard announces itself before it can hurt you - into a Godot project. I will write the shader that does the announcing by hand; you write the driver and the tests that prove it.
props.label: RECONSTRUCTION

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 2/4 - hesitant writer, one working single-word correction with measured time to complete it.
beats.narration_text: Here is what actually changed. A spike trap that turns - correction - that ramps red across four tenths of a second before it fires. Two materials from one shader, on two identical slimes. And a three-pixel image, sampled twice through the same file, that settles an argument about colour. Ninety-nine automated checks stand behind that, and four deliberate breakages stand behind the checks.

props.title: What was built
lines: 4 mutations, each caught by a different net
Every predicted pixel committed before it was measured

beats.role_note: C1 CODE. trap_warning.gdshader in full, hand-written. Paired with B03.
beats.narration_text: This is the whole shader. Four lines of declaration and one line that changes a colour. Mix takes the pixel the sprite already has, the warning red, and a number between them. The number is not time - it is game state, and it arrives from outside. The window is four tenths of a second, and the detection box that starts it is one seven five - not a number anybody chose, but the walking speed multiplied by that window. Note what the first argument is: COLOR, not a texture sample. COLOR already carries the sprite's texture multiplied by its modulate. Sampling the texture again by hand would throw that multiplication away, and a trap the game had faded out would ignore the fade entirely.

props.title: One line changes the colour

notes.label: Why COLOR, not TEXTURE
notes.value: COLOR arrives as texture x modulate x vertex colour. Re-sampling discards two of the three.

notes.label: Why not TIME
notes.value: TIME is global engine time. It cannot express time since THIS trap armed.

cues.label: the warning red, set by the material
the one line that changes a colour

beats.role_note: C1 RESULT. take-w, trap 1's cycle. The log puts the warning at frame 109, t 1.82, player_x 174.4; the window runs 0.30-4.85 s so the footage outlasts the narration.
beats.narration_text: There it is. Red before the player arrives, spikes while they are standing on it.

show.event: the trap is flush and nearly invisible
the red begins, player still short of it

beats.role_note: C2 CODE. trap_warning_driver.gd 62-76, agent-written. Paired with B05.
beats.narration_text: The shader is the author's; this driver is not. It does two things. It duplicates the material, because a sub-resource inside a packed scene is shared by every instance of that scene - without this line all three traps hold one material and warn together. Then, once a frame, it copies the trap's state into the uniform. It reads game state and never writes it. And it asks the shader whether that uniform exists, because setting a name the shader does not declare writes nowhere and reports nothing.

props.title: One material per trap, one write per frame
props.code:
# R6. duplicate() is shallow, which is what is wanted: the Shader itself
	# stays shared (it is read-only program text) while the parameter block
	# becomes this trap's own.
	material = shared.duplicate() as ShaderMaterial
	_sprite.material = material

	uniform_declared = _declares(material.shader, UNIFORM_WARN)
	if not uniform_declared:
		push_error("Shader does not declare a uniform named '%s'; every write from this driver would be discarded in silence." % UNIFORM_WARN)


func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	if material == null:
		return
	material.set_shader_parameter(UNIFORM_WARN, _trap.warn_amount)

notes.label: F1, avoided
notes.value: Sub-resources are shared across scene instances. Without duplicate() one red lights all three.

notes.label: F5, caught at startup
notes.value: set_shader_parameter on an undeclared name is silent. The driver asks the shader instead.

cues.label: ask the shader what it declares
state in, uniform out, once a frame

beats.role_note: C2 RESULT. take-w across all three traps, 0.60-11.40 s. The take's own probe counted zero frames in 709 with more than one trap lit.
beats.narration_text: Watch the red move. Three traps, one shader, three materials - and the warning never appears on two at once. The driver counted it: seven hundred and nine frames, zero with more than one lit.

show.event: trap one warns, two and three stay flush
trap three, and the first two are dark

beats.role_note: C3 CODE. hint_bands.gdshader 1-7, hand-written. Paired with B07.
beats.narration_text: Two samplers. The same file is bound to both. The only difference between them is four words on line four - source colour - and a boolean picks which one reaches the screen. Unshaded matters here: without it the light would scale the result and the numbers would measure the lamp instead of the sampler. Nearest filtering matters too, because the image is three pixels wide and linear filtering would blend the answer.

props.title: The same file, sampled two ways

notes.label: Why unshaded
notes.value: Any lighting multiplies ALBEDO and the measured band stops being a statement about the sampler.

notes.label: Why nearest
notes.value: The image is 3 x 1. Linear filtering averages neighbouring bands and no predicted value survives.

beats.role_note: C3 RESULT. captures/a5/hint_experiment.png, real windowed run. All six bands exact against the prediction committed on 2026-10-23.
beats.narration_text: Both quads, one frame. The file stores sixty four, one twenty eight and one ninety two. Through the sampler that decodes, those are the numbers that come out - decoding and the display's encoding are inverses. Through the one that does not, every band is brighter: one thirty seven, one eighty eight, two twenty five. All six were predicted in writing two days before anything could render them, and all six landed exactly.

show.event: 64 -> 137 is marked as the largest error

props.title: The hint is worth seventy three counts
props.imageLabel: engine capture above, recorded numbers below, rendered verbatim

beats.role_note: C4 CODE. dungeon_surface.gdshader fragment, lines 15-27, hand-written. Paired with B09. Author's comments are in Chinese and shown verbatim.
beats.narration_text: The spatial shader. One read from the mask, one read from the stone, and then two outputs. Albedo gets the stone darkened where the mask says water pools. Roughness is mixed between a dry value and a wet one by the same mask. Two numbers written, and Godot does the lighting - in plain GLSL the whole reflectance model would be yours to write. The mask is data, not a picture: its numbers mean how submerged, not how bright.

props.title: Two outputs, one mask

notes.label: Data, not a picture
notes.value: wetness_mask is sampled without source_color. Decoded, 0.5 would become 0.21 and the waterline would move.

notes.label: What Godot does next
notes.value: ALBEDO and ROUGHNESS feed the engine's lighting. Plain GLSL would make you write the BRDF.

cues.label: dry to wet, by the same mask

beats.role_note: C4 RESULT. captures/a5/materials/00-baseline.png under section 8's lighting. Sweep numbers from captures/a5/materials/SWEEP-REPORT.txt.
beats.narration_text: Same mesh, same light, same shader. The difference is three values in a text file. The right-hand slime is darker, slightly green, and carries a sharp highlight where the dry one is matte - that highlight is roughness nought point nought eight. Across twelve sweep captures the dry slime measured fifty, fifty six, fifty five every single time, unchanged to the count, while the flooded one moved for every uniform. One material, one object.

show.event: the highlight on the flooded slime is marked

props.title: One shader, two materials
props.imageLabel: engine capture above, two of the four swept uniforms below

beats.role_note: C5 CODE. hint_bands.gdshader lines 4-5, the two samplers at reading size. The mutation deleted source_color from line 4 and was restored. Paired with B11.
beats.narration_text: Back to those two lines. Delete source colour from the first one and nothing complains. The shader still compiles. There is no shader error in the log. And here is the part that matters: ask the engine to describe both uniforms and it returns the same answer for each - type twenty four, hint seventeen, texture two D. The engine cannot see this hint on a sampler at all. On a vector three it can. So a test built on the uniform list passes while the thing it was written to protect is gone.

show.event: the two lines are shown as identical to the engine

props.title: The hint the engine cannot see
props.code:
uniform sampler2D bands_srgb : source_color, filter_nearest;
uniform sampler2D bands_data : filter_nearest;

notes.label: What the engine reports
notes.value: stone_albedo and wetness_mask both come back type 24, hint 17, 'Texture2D'. Identical.

notes.label: The asymmetry
notes.value: On a vec3 the same keyword IS visible - TYPE_COLOR with COLOR_NO_ALPHA instead of TYPE_VECTOR3.

cues.label: and this line is now its twin

beats.role_note: C5 RESULT. evidence/a5-mutations/mutation3a-hint-sampler_capture.png, the capture taken with the mutation in place. Restored afterwards.
beats.narration_text: This is the same scene with those four words gone. Both quads now read one thirty seven, one eighty eight, two twenty five. The two sides of the experiment have become identical and its entire result has disappeared - silently. No error, no warning, no change in the uniform list. The only thing that caught it was a test that reads the shader's source text, and the suite now asserts the blindness itself so nobody simplifies that check away later.

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 3/4 - verdict. Implemented work, limitations and human judgment kept apart. Human/AI split stated.
beats.narration_text: So. Written by hand, by the author: three shaders and the language notes. Written by Claude: the driver, four test suites, the capture rigs and the material audit. Measured, not asserted: eight predicted pixels exact, six predicted bands exact, and hint range does not clamp a value set from code - two point zero passed straight through and the pixel went pure red. What no headless run established: any of it. The dummy renderer draws nothing, so every colour claim here came from a windowed capture on real hardware. Still open: the slice has no audio and no art beyond code-drawn blocks, and that port is Assignment Six's first job.

columns.heading: Still open
items: no normal map, so no curl check

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 4/4 - Your Turn. One bounded change with a prediction, not blind copying. Liam signs off here.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take the prompt on screen, then do the bounded version yourself: open the warning shader, change nothing, and predict what the base plate pixel becomes at a warning of nought point five. Mix is linear - the arithmetic is one line. Then set it from code and capture the frame in engine, not with a screenshot tool, and see whether your number survives contact. If it does not, that is a finding, not a mistake. Write down which one you trust and why. Liam, signing off.

props.command: Please use Walker to add a second controlled value to my shader capture rig, write the predicted pixel into the brief before the rig can run, and tell me plainly if the capture disagrees with what I wrote.
